# Branches the prune may delete even though the automatic test says keep.
#
# The test in prune-branches.yml is deliberately blunt: a branch survives if it
# carries a single commit that main does not. That is right by default, and it
# is wrong for a branch whose extra commit went in under a *different* branch —
# a chain, where each branch was started from the last one before its PR merged.
# Every line below was checked by hand and the reason recorded.
#
# Format: <branch> # <why it is safe to delete>
# Lines are consumed exactly; a typo means the branch is simply not deleted.

claude/access-levels-3                # extra commit landed as PR #175 (claude/fix-restricted-sliders)
claude/attendance-empty-state         # extra commit is the merge of PR #183; no content diff against main
claude/club-dir-dept-contacts         # extra commit rebuilds club-roster/, a directory main no longer has
claude/contacts-linked-lock           # extra commit landed as PR #222 (claude/contacts-select-force)
claude/contacts-multi-role            # extra commit landed as PR #219 (claude/contacts-roles-clean)
claude/contacts-roles-clean           # club-contacts v2.0 against v2.31 on main; the CSS fix was superseded
claude/contacts-roles-v2              # never had a PR; same commit as contacts-multi-role's tip, which is in main
claude/entry-route-convert-e0wang     # PR #865 closed unmerged; the work landed as PR #870
claude/fix-restricted-sliders         # extra commit landed as PR #176 (claude/tp-invite-staff-lock)
claude/gas-pending-live-edits-e0wang  # PR #861 closed unmerged; superseded by PR #862
claude/stadium-data-2026              # extra commit landed as PR #141 (claude/clubs-meta-optaids)
